subject: Control plane egress & allowlist — Nexus Private Endpoint handoff
messages:
From: Ethan Scott <ethan.scott@nexalus.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Nexalus Compliance <compliance@nexalus.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint allowlist request — control plane + telemetry egress

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the private deployment run-through today. Nexalus is close to finishing the network design for our VPC-connected private runtime; compliance needs an explicit allowlist and firewall policy for Redwood's control plane and update/telemetry endpoints before we sign off. A few items for us to confirm: 

- Do you publish a small set of static egress IPs we can NAT to for control plane/control-channel? If not, what are the recommended fallback models (regional pools, ephemeral NATs)?
- What TCP/UDP ports and FQDNs are required for: control-plane, telemetry/usage, image/asset pull (model snapshots), and OS/package updates on private nodes?
- Do you support a customer-side outbound proxy / TLS-inspecting middlebox? If yes, any mTLS or cert pinning requirements?
- We also need evidence for the allowlist request (IP list + short design notes) to attach to our audit.

Can you send the requested list + a short note on expected failover behavior (if an IP rotates) and any recommended staleness/refresh cadence?

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Scott
Head of Infrastructure, Nexalus

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Scott <ethan.scott@nexalus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint allowlist request — control plane + telemetry egress

Ethan — great to meet earlier. High level answers up front, then Laura and Marissa are copied to provide the more formal evidence pack.

- Static IPs: For Hosted control plane connections we offer a small set of static egress IPs per region when customers opt into "Dedicated control egress" (recommended for audit-heavy customers). If you choose the standard private endpoint route, we provide short-lived regional IP ranges with a documented rotation/refresh window.

- Ports/FQDNs: Minimal set is TCP 443 outbound to our control-plane FQDNs, plus TCP 443 to s3/redwood-artifact endpoints for model snapshot pulls. Telemetry is pushed over HTTPS as well. Laura, I'll let you paste the canonical port/FQDN matrix.

- Proxy/mTLS: We support customer outbound proxies. We recommend TLS pass-through for control-plane traffic by default to preserve end-to-end TLS, but can support mTLS if you can terminate and re-origin certs on your proxy. Certificate pinning is optional but we do publish our cert rotation schedule.

I'll attach a CSV with the current control-plane IPs (for the Dedicated control egress option) and a short checklist. Marissa — can you attach the evidence PDF and confirm SOC2 references?

Next steps:
1) Alex -> attach current CSV of static IPs for OA region (attached).
2) Marissa -> supply attestation PDF + compliance snippet.
3) Laura -> confirm ports + fallback behavior and whether we require SNI passthrough or specific ALPN.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---Attachment: redwood-controlplane-egress-ips.csv (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Scott <ethan.scott@nexalus.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint allowlist request — control plane + telemetry egress

Ethan — adding the compliance artifacts you requested. Attached is a short evidence pack (safelist-evidence.pdf) that maps our control plane services to the audit categories your team typically asks for (networking, control-channel, telemetry retention). A few clarifications: 

- If you opt for Dedicated control egress we'll provide a /29 set for the control plane (stable for 90 days, rotated with notice). If you run the private control plane with customer NAT addresses, we'll accept any static NAT you present — but we ask that you notify us 72 hours before changing the NAT address.
- For customers using an outbound proxy with TLS inspection, our stated preference is: terminate TLS to the proxy only if you can do mTLS to our control plane endpoints. Otherwise use pass-through.
- Evidence: we've included a redacted SOC 2 network diagram in the PDF and a short description of our telemetry retention policy (30 days aggregated token metrics by default; options for 90/365 with an enterprise add-on).

I'll also attach an XLS with port mappings for quick firewall entries.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if your security ops want to run through the document.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

---Attachments: safelist-evidence.pdf (stub), egress-telemetry-matrix.xlsx (stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Scott <ethan.scott@nexalus.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint allowlist request — control plane + telemetry egress

Ethan — following up with the engineering/security details you should include in your firewall policy and allowlist. I included inline examples you can paste into a policy management ticket.

1) Minimal egress allowed list (customer NAT -> Redwood):
   - TCP 443 -> control01.cp.redwood-inference.com (resolve to IPs below)
   - TCP 443 -> artifacts.redwood-inference.com (S3-backed, used for model downloads)
   - TCP 443 -> telemetry.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS ingestion only)

   Static IPs (Dedicated control egress option): 34.210.45.120/32, 34.210.45.121/32, 34.210.45.122/32 (these three are the current /29 sample; formal CSV attached). If you select standard private routing we will publish a regional CIDR and a rotation schedule.

2) Ports and protocols:
   - Outbound TCP 443 only. No inbound ports needed.
   - DNS to your resolver allowed for FQDN resolution (UDP/TCP 53) — Redwood will not rely on reverse DNS to gate control traffic.

3) Proxy / TLS inspection notes: 
   - We recommend TLS pass-through for control-channel. If your security team must perform TLS termination, configure the outbound proxy to do mTLS to our endpoints and provide us with the proxy cert fingerprint ahead of time. Without mTLS we cannot guarantee control channel integrity for signed payloads.

4) Failover and rotation behavior: 
   - If you use the Dedicated egress IPs we publish, we will provide 7 days notice before IP changes (emergency rotation may be shorter; in that case we'll notify via both email and support portal). For ephemeral/regional pools, the client should be configured to refresh DNS every 60s and to have a fallback for up to 10s retry windows.

5) Observability & telemetry egress: 
   - Telemetry endpoints only accept authenticated HTTPS with token rotation. No additional ports required. If you want to block telemetry from leaving the VPC for any reason, we can provide an offline mode for diagnostic builds but note that autoscaling/health checks will be impaired.

6) Suggested firewall rule templates (paste to infra ticket):
   - Allow outbound TCP/443 to control01.cp.redwood-inference.com (resolve to 34.210.45.120, .121, .122)
   - Allow outbound TCP/443 to artifacts.redwood-inference.com (S3 endpoints — list in attached XLS)
   - Allow DNS resolution (UDP/TCP 53) to authorized resolvers only

Action items:
- Ethan: confirm whether Nexalus will use Dedicated control egress (we'll reserve the /29) or customer NAT addresses.
- Nexalus security: if performing TLS inspection, send the proxy cert fingerprint and we will validate and enable mTLS on our side.
- Alex/Marissa: schedule a 30-minute ops sync w/ Nexalus SecOps this week.

I'll keep the attachments in the Drive link Marissa shared. Let me know if you need the control-plane IPs in a signed SLA form.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

---Attachment references: redwood-controlplane-egress-ips.csv, egress-telemetry-matrix.xlsx, safelist-evidence.pdf
